Sergio — thanks for the demo yesterday. Aurora's evaluation lead asked for a short mutual action plan we can use internally (procurement + clinical ops) that calls out: evaluation milestones, acceptance criteria, and a realistic timing window for Dedicated vs Private deployments (we have some on-prem air-gapped sites).

High level asks from our side:
- Evaluation cadence (3-week sprint? 6-week pilot?)
- Required artifacts (SOC2, data handling, logs)
- A clear commit runway: how long from sign to having a Dedicated GPU pool vs private on-prem staging ready
- A first-pass GPU pool sizing recommendation based on targeted throughput: ~200 concurrent patient sessions, median response length 600 tokens, peak concurrency 350

Can you and your ops/procurement counterpart put something informal together this week? Procurement will need dates to feed into their supplier calendar.

Best,

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: AuroraHealth MAP — evaluation -> ops handshake and GPU pool timing

Thanks Daphne — absolutely. I pulled together a concise MAP draft (high-level) and looped in Ben (commercial/dedicated terms), Marissa (onboarding/acceptance milestones) and Karthik (capacity/sizing).

Quick summary up front (we'll attach a spreadsheet):
1) Suggested evaluation run: 4-week pilot (2-week integration + 2-week capacity/quality ramp).
2) Acceptance criteria: 95% of responses under 600ms P50 for median sessions during pilot, qualitative clinical sign-off on 200 sampled summaries, and no PII leakage > 0 incidents in trial logs.
3) Typical lead times:
   - Dedicated (Redwood-managed GPU pool, reserved capacity): target delivery 6–10 weeks after contract execution (depends on region and tranche scheduling; US-west tends to be faster).
   - Private (customer-managed VPC or on-prem): 10–16 weeks for on-prem hardware procurement + staging + security review; private VPC deployments (cloud-hosted but customer VPC) typically 6–12 weeks.
   - Fast-start option: we can provide hosted capacity in 3–5 business days for the eval to avoid blocking momentum while Dedicated/Private are provisioned.
4) First-pass GPU pool sizing (ballpark for 200 concurrent sessions; median response 600 tokens):
   - Option A (latency-prioritized): 8 x A100-80GB equiv GPUs (sized for P50 < 600ms, supports batching/kv optimizations).
   - Option B (cost-balanced): 5 x A100-80GB equiv + quantized 4-bit model variants and aggressive prefix caching — P50 ~800ms, much lower cost.
   - We recommend starting with Option B for evaluation and scaling to Option A for production if latency/regulatory needs require it.

I attached a quick spreadsheet with scenario math and a SOC2 evidence stub. Ben — can you add high-level commercial cadence and procurement milestones? Marissa/Karthik — suggest we include staging acceptance gates and an ops handshake: who owns the cutover, rollback plan, and model pinning policy.

I'll convert this into a MAP doc and timeline and get it back to you by Monday. If procurement needs a sketch timeline sooner, say so and we'll push an interim summary.

Cheers,
Sergio

--
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Accounts | Redwood Inference

- Contracting lead times: legal and procurement reviews typically 2–3 weeks at your end; we can prepare a skeleton MSA + SOW quickly.
- Financial carve-outs: we can structure an initial pilot invoice and then apply credits to the committed monthly amount upon conversion (helps bridge the eval period).

I'll also add a high level milestone table to the MAP:

  - T+3d: Hosted eval capacity available (temporary)

  - T+6–10w: Dedicated pool delivery (if Dedicated chosen)

Attaching a template MAP (MAP_Aurora_v1.xlsx) and a sizing CSV. Sergio — if we can get your ops-runbook bullets in the sheet, I'll feed these to procurement as a timeline.

Daphne — quick ops excerpt below (happy to expand into the MAP sheet):

Ops-runbook excerpt (canary + acceptance):
- Canary window: 72 hours with progressive ramp (1% -> 10% -> 50%), monitoring dashboards live in Redwood Console.
- Acceptance scripts: "acceptance_latency.py" (measures P50/P95 over sample window), "content_fidelity_check.sh" (randomly samples 200 outputs and verifies clinical template compliance).
- Rollback window & plan: immediate rollback trigger if any of the following occur during canary: P95 latency > 2.5s for more than 10 minutes, >2 critical clinical template failures, or any high-severity security incident. Rollback is handled by pinning traffic to previous model variant and draining new variant tokens.

Notes on lead times and hybrid path:
- Dedicated billing: we support monthly invoicing but the committed capacity discount assumes a minimum 6-month billing/commit. We can do a 3-month rolling for your first tranche with a minor pricing uplift (Ben will inline pricing options).
- Data residency: hosted eval can be provisioned in EU region; we will enable EU-residency for any datasets stored for pilot. For on-prem or private VPC, residency is controlled by customer network.

I'll attach these bullets into the MAP file and drop a version link in the Drive folder. Let us know if procurement needs a compact one-page timeline — we can produce a single-slide timeline for their supplier calendar.

Marissa
Onboarding & Solutions | Redwood Inference
